action_items: (LOW, carry-over iter14) PortalLayout.jsx mobile <select> renders <span> badges inside <option>, React hydration warning (non-blocking).
(LOW, carry-over iter7-15) server.py is now ~6886 lines. Splitting into routers (auth/admin/portal/forms/whatsapp/scheduler/automations/templates/timeline/db) is overdue.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py admin_client_timeline (~1110-1252) is a clean single-endpoint aggregator — 5 independent motor queries (one per collection), each gated on the 'wanted' set so ?types= filtering happens PRE-query (efficient) not post-hoc. The counts are then computed after the final limit cap, which correctly matches the 'counts reflect only what's returned' contract verified by tests.

server.py timeline sort uses string ISO sort (`x.get('ts') or ''`) — relies on all ts values being ISO-8601 strings. Works correctly because every insert in the codebase (appointments.scheduled_at, interventions.intervention_date/created_at, whatsapp_messages.created_at, form_submissions.created_at, documents.created_at) writes isoformat() strings. However, if any legacy doc has ts=None OR a datetime object (e.g. from a direct mongo migration), `None` sorts to the end (empty string) and datetime vs str comparison would TypeError. The `or ''` defends against None but not type mismatch. LOW priority — all current writes are strings.

server.py timeline wraps the documents query in try/except Exception: pass — defensive because the documents collection schema is unstable (client_id vs owner_id vs uploaded_by). Acceptable but silently swallows real errors; consider logging.warning for visibility.
server.py timeline forms batch-resolution (~1188-1195) does ONE follow-up query per unique form_id set — scales O(k) where k=distinct forms. Nice, no N+1.

server.py timeline whatsapp status mapping: `status: 'ok' if m.get('ok') else 'ko'` — drives frontend's emerald/rose color pill. Confirmed: both the ok=True seed (status='ok', emerald) and the 'ko' fallback path render correctly per the frontend color-coding logic in AdminClientTimeline.jsx.

AdminClientTimeline.jsx uses Object.entries(TYPE_META) to render the 5 filter pills in a stable order — matches backend's 5 counts keys. The pill `active` state toggles the Tailwind class between `${meta.color} text-white` and `bg-white text-slate-600 border-slate-300` — matches spec ('colored when active, gray/white-bg when inactive'). Verified programmatically by reading class before/after click.
AdminClients.jsx adds a `<Link to={`/admin/clients/${c.id}/timeline`}>` with Activity icon per row + data-testid='timeline-client-<id>' — lightweight and reuses existing row layout. Good.

AdminClientTimeline.jsx grouped-by-month rendering uses French locale 'MMMM yyyy' (toLocaleDateString('fr-FR', {month:'long', year:'numeric'})) — correctly produced 'avril 2026' header in the screenshot. One caveat: if ts parsing ever returns Invalid Date, Object.entries(grouped) would show 'Invalid Date' key — consider a fallback to 'Sans date' in the groupBy step (LOW).

context_for_next_testing_agent: Timeline regression suite is /app/backend/tests/test_sawali_iter16.py (11 tests, ~3s). Seeding pattern: insert docs directly via pymongo with {id, client_id, created_at, ...source-specific-fields} — each collection has slightly different schema (appointments.scheduled_at, interventions.intervention_date+intervention_number, whatsapp_messages.template_name+ok, form_submissions.form_id→resolved via forms.id, documents.name+size+category). Remember to also seed a matching forms doc if you want a nice form title; otherwise the endpoint falls back to 'Soumission formulaire'. Auth: 401 for no token, 403 for any non-admin (including the client themselves using their own token). The endpoint filters ?types= PRE-query (efficient) and computes counts POST-filter. Default limit=200, ?limit=N caps results. Frontend testids are exactly as spec: timeline-client-<id> on AdminClients rows, client-timeline-page on route, timeline-back / timeline-refresh / timeline-filter-<type> / timeline-list / timeline-event-<type>-<id>.
rca of the issue: No bugs found in iter16. The unified CRM timeline — backend aggregator (5 source collections, 'wanted' gating for ?types filter, batch form-title resolution, string-ISO DESC sort, post-filter counts, 404 for unknown client, admin-only auth) AND the AdminClientTimeline.jsx UI (5 filter pills with count badges and color-toggle on click, month-grouped vertical timeline with colored badge markers + relative datetime + color-coded status pills, back link, refresh button) AND the AdminClients.jsx row button with Activity icon linking to the timeline route — all match the spec exactly. The seed-1-of-each pattern in pytest verifies the endpoint genuinely queries all 5 collections (not stubs). The documents query's $or:[{client_id},{owner_id},{uploaded_by}] was exercised by the {client_id: uid} seed variant and worked.
